title: Amateur radio flashcards: for the FCC Technician exam (2026–2030 pool)
description: Every question of the 2026–2030 Technician Class (Element 2) question pool as flashcards, with the units, radio waves, rules, operating practice, electronics, signals, propagation, antennas and safety each one needs, each idea taught before it is tested.
notice: Questions marked 'Pool' are from the 2026–2030 Technician question pool, released into the public domain by the NCVEC Question Pool Committee. Also contains material from 47 CFR Parts 1, 2 and 97, US Government works in the public domain. This deck is independent and is not affiliated with, sponsored, endorsed or approved by the FCC, the NCVEC or any VEC.

changelog.notes: First draft, not yet released: awaiting the independent audit, a newcomer read-through and an expert review.

glossary.AMSAT: Radio Amateur Satellite Corporation, and similar amateur satellite organisations
glossary.BNC: a quick-connect, twist-to-lock RF connector for coaxial cable
glossary.CFR: Code of Federal Regulations (for example, 47 CFR Part 97 holds the amateur radio rules)
glossary.DB: as in DB-25, a D-subminiature computer data connector
glossary.DNA: deoxyribonucleic acid, which carries the genetic instructions of living things
glossary.DRM: Digital Radio Mondiale, a digital broadcasting system
glossary.DX: distance or distant (telegraphic shorthand); DX stations are distant stations
glossary.F2: the F2 layer, the upper part of the ionosphere’s F region
glossary.IEEE: Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers
glossary.J3E: emission designator: single-sideband, suppressed carrier (J), one channel of analogue information (3), telephony (E)
glossary.KA1X: an example call sign in pool question T1C05
glossary.KF1XXX: an example call sign in pool question T1C05
glossary.KL7CC: an example call sign in the pool
glossary.NCVEC: National Conference of Volunteer Examiner Coordinators
glossary.NOT: not (the pool writes it in capitals for emphasis)
glossary.PACTOR: a radio data mode used by amateur radio operators
glossary.PL: as in PL-259, the threaded plug of the UHF connector family
glossary.PSK31: Phase Shift Keying, 31 baud: a keyboard-to-keyboard text mode
glossary.QRN: Q signal: I am troubled by static
glossary.QRU: Q signal: have you anything for me?
glossary.QRZ: Q signal: who is calling me?
glossary.QSB: Q signal: your signals are fading
glossary.QSL: Q signal: I am acknowledging receipt
glossary.QSO: Q signal: I can communicate with … direct; amateurs use it for a contact
glossary.QSR: Q signal: repeat your call on the calling frequency
glossary.QSY: Q signal: change to transmission on another frequency
glossary.QTC: Q signal: I have … messages for you
glossary.R3E: emission designator: single-sideband, reduced or variable-level carrier (R), one channel of analogue information (3), telephony (E)
glossary.RG: the prefix of coaxial cable type names, as in RG-58 and RG-213
glossary.RPT: an indicator offered as a wrong answer in pool question T1F05
glossary.RS: as in “RS-213”, a wrong answer in pool question T9B06: no such connector
glossary.STAR: as in D-STAR, a digital voice and data protocol for amateur radio
glossary.VTVM: a type of voltmeter, named in a wrong answer of pool question T7C02
glossary.W1XX: an example call sign in pool question T1C05
glossary.W3: a self-assigned indicator, as in KL7CC/W3
glossary.WSJT: a family of weak-signal amateur radio programs; WSJT-X is the current one

checks.what: Three independent audits read all 1012 cards against the 2026–2030 Technician pool, 47 CFR and the other cited sources, for accuracy and for plain language, and checked every figure
checks.result: All 409 pool questions are verbatim with the correct key. Six wrong explanations, 8 unsupported claims, 5 ambiguous cards, 22 unclear ones and 252 minor issues were fixed; about 260 explanations were rewritten to give the reason; 30 of 31 Wikipedia-sourced cards now cite public-domain primary sources.
